A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MS-Temba and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. The complete 13-page v1 and 14-page v2 support comparison, including content relocated between the main text and supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original MS-Temba benchmark results, efficiency measurements, qualitative predictions, and ablations on TSU, MultiTHUMOS, and Charades, including supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds edge-device measurements and a qualitative comparison with multimodal language models.

M1.justification: The architecture, dilated bidirectional scanning, feature fusion, classification head, and BCE objective are retained. TLM becomes TCM, DTS becomes D-SSM, and Temporal Mamba Fuser becomes Scale-Aware State Fuser; their described operations and supplementary architecture specifications remain equivalent.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate densely labeled temporal action detection on TSU, MultiTHUMOS, and Charades. The added device experiment and language-model comparison do not establish a new dataset, population, or input-task scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds PointTAD, HAAN, and DualDETR to the I3D comparison. The new edge experiment compares against MS-TCT and a linear classifier, while Figure 11 evaluates VideoLLaVA and TimeChat qualitatively. Together these substantially broaden the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: v2 adds a bounded edge-device evaluation using an NVIDIA Jetson Nano described as having 8GB memory and a 15W configuration, reporting training latency, memory, power, and mAP. Figure 11 also introduces a prompted language-model comparison. Existing benchmark settings and supplementary training configurations are retained.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section 11 and Figure 11 add a qualitative case examining VideoLLaVA and TimeChat localization failures. Existing component, dilation, scanning, block-count, layer-count, and temporal-downsampling analyses remain. Moving the downsampling analysis into the main text and redrawing the existing localization example do not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for model performance. Averaging information density over ten videos and reporting action-duration standard deviations are retained practices.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores are retained, but substantial comparison and deployment results are added. Table 1 adds DualDETR at 45.5 MultiTHUMOS mAP versus MS-Temba's unchanged 43.7 with I3D. New Table 3 reports edge training latency of 4.2 versus 10.6 seconds and power of 8 versus 11.2 watts for MS-Temba versus MS-TCT. These are additional results under distinct conditions, not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The continuous SSM equation is corrected from h'(t) = Ah(t) + Ax(t) in v1 Equation 1 to h'(t) = Ah(t) + Bx(t) in v2 Equation 10. The remaining mathematical content is retained, including the preliminaries moved to the supplement; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about efficient multiscale TAD and long-video performance persist. v2 adds explicit claims that naive Mamba adaptation is ineffective and that MS-Temba supports direct training and deployment on edge devices, extending the practical contribution beyond v1's efficiency argument.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation that naive Mamba adaptation loses local information through state compression, interprets the new device measurements as evidence of deployment suitability, and discusses timestamp, concurrency, and resource limitations of multimodal language models. Existing interpretations of dilation, downsampling, and CLIP feature density are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the edge-device model, memory capacity, and power configuration, explicitly marks the backbone as frozen in Figure 2, and supplies the language-model query in Figure 11. Existing training hyperparameters, architecture tables, desktop hardware information, and code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds recent TAD references, including PointTAD, HAAN, and DualDETR, alongside VMamba, MViTv2, and video-language-model literature. It explicitly acknowledges prior local-global and multiscale learning while positioning its contribution as their SSM adaptation for TAD. The central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten, component terminology changes throughout the main text, and five boxed findings organize the narrative. Preliminaries, feature-density analysis, and qualitative evaluation move to the supplement, while temporal-downsampling analysis moves into the main text.

P2.justification: Figures 1-5 are substantially redrawn, and v2 adds the edge-device table and language-model comparison figure. The two information-density plots are merged onto a normalized horizontal axis, existing plots and the qualitative example are restyled, and numerous tables and figures are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful contemporary baselines and direct edge-device evidence where v1 relied on desktop efficiency measurements, while clearer architecture diagrams and the corrected SSM equation improve exposition and correctness. The gain is limited by incomplete specification of the edge experiment and broad language-model limitations supported by one qualitative example. The core benchmark and ablation evidence remains unchanged.
